text:
maria: Heads up — seeing cross-request contamination from the KV cache on staging. Repro with streaming + paging on long contexts (>12k tokens).

maria: Quick log excerpt: 
```
[KVCache] load_block id=42 seq=128 offset=0 len=512 owner=session=abc123
[KVCache] apply_kv seq=128 start_token=512 -> applied tokens from owner=abc123 to session=def456
model output: ... <token 23> (from previous session)
```

sunil: ugh. Which model and build? any repro steps?

maria: staging: redwood-inference:staging-2026-03-10, gpt-medium-quant. Repro sequence: start session s1 generate ~8k tokens, close, then start s2 streaming request; s2 output occasionally includes tokens that only existed in s1.

maria: repro curl:
```
# s1
curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood/v1/streams \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGING" \
  -H "x-session-id: s1" \
  -d '{"prompt": "long chat... (repeat)"}'
# s2
curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood/v1/streams \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGING" \
  -H "x-session-id: s2" \
  -d '{"prompt": "short follow-up"}'
```

keiko: could be an offset/alignment bug when we page and partially fill blocks. If a page gets split across two owners, our copy logic uses absolute_offsets but then applies relative offsets when reading, so you can end up shifting by block_size. I suspect off-by-one in the memcpy window.

dave: ran a microbench: memory growth shows linear ramp with context length and fragmentation spikes at page boundaries. flamegraph snapshot: https://internal.artifacts/redwood/flame/kv-paging-20260310.svg (perm link) — notable GC-like pauses when we recompact.

ryan: I reproduced locally. test_kv_alignment_randomized.py fails ~1/500 runs with deterministic seed 83421. Stack points to kv_pager::apply_block -> copy_range. Adding an owner check stops the failure (quick hack).

maria: i pushed a canary that adds owner_id verification before reusing a block. deploy-canary -> staging.

infra-bot: deploy: canary/staging/redwood-inference:staging-2026-03-10 -> success (node pool a3, 3/3).

maria: canary looks clean for cross-request leakage — no contamination across 200 runs. Perf hit is ~+1.8ms p50 on small requests, negligible for long contexts.

keiko: plan: 1) add strict owner_id check + invalidate on mismatch (short term) 2) rewrite copy_range to use safe-aligned memmoves and explicit offsets (medium) 3) add randomized interleaved-session soak test (long). Also add metrics: kv_block_owner_mismatch_count and kv_cache_stale_evictions.

ryan: I'll open PR with owner check + unit tests (will include the failing seed). Link: https://git.redwood/pr/eng-runtime/kv-owner-guard.

dave: i'll run a 24h soak on staging with bursty interleaved sessions and measure latency/fragmentation.

maria: assigning eng-runtime ownership. Will monitor canary and roll forward after 6h if green.

keiko: also add a lint rule to avoid implicit offset math in kv pager code.

maria: thanks team. Filing internal incident and epic. Ticket: RW-8762 (KV cache owner/alignment bug).

maria: ping @sunil @dave @keiko if you spot regressions during the soak.
